findings.title: Potential NullPointerException when getResourceTypeResource returns null
findings.body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, when no specific resource is found for the client, the code calls `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. This method can return null (e.g., if `supportsAuthorizationSchema` returns false internally, or if the 'Clients' type resource was never created). The result is then immediately dereferenced on line 219 with `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()`, which will throw a NullPointerException if `resource` is null. A null check should be added after the call to `getResourceTypeResource`.

findings.title: registerListener will call setPermissionsEnabled which throws UnsupportedOperationException in V2 mode
findings.body: The `registerListener` method now gates event handling behind `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`. However, when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled (which is the focus of this PR), `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`, whose `clients()` returns `ClientPermissionsV2`. The `setPermissionsEnabled` method in `ClientPermissionsV2` (line 193) throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. If both V1 and V2 features are enabled simultaneously (which is typical since V2 builds on V1), removing a client will trigger this listener and cause an unhandled `UnsupportedOperationException`, breaking client deletion. The same applies to `roles().setPermissionsEnabled` and `groups().setPermissionsEnabled` if their V2 implementations also throw.

findings.title: Dead code: getEvaluationContext method is never called
findings.body: The private method `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel authorizedClient, AccessToken token)` at line 262 is never invoked anywhere in the class. The `canExchangeTo` method that would logically use it throws `UnsupportedOperationException` instead. This dead code, along with the unused imports (`EvaluationContext`, `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `AccessToken`, `Scope`, and the static import of `TOKEN_EXCHANGE`), should be removed to avoid confusion.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle CLIENTS resource type, may return null
findings.body: The `getResourceName` method handles the USERS resource type by resolving the username, but does not handle the newly added CLIENTS resource type. For client resources, the resource name is set to the client's internal ID (from `resolveClient`). The method falls through to `return resource.getDisplayName()` which may return null if no display name was explicitly set on the resource (the `resourceStore.create` call in `getOrCreateResource` does not set a display name). This could result in null being returned where a human-readable name is expected in the UI or API responses.

findings.title: canMapRoles does not check MANAGE_CLIENTS admin role unlike other methods
findings.body: In `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles`, the code only checks fine-grained permissions via `hasPermission(client, ...)`. Unlike `canManage(ClientModel)` which first checks `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)`, these methods do not check any admin role. In V1 (`ClientPermissions`), `canMapRoles` checks for `MANAGE_CLIENTS` role first. If this asymmetry is unintentional, an admin with `MANAGE_CLIENTS` role but without explicit FGAP `map-roles` permission would be unable to map client roles in V2 mode, which is a behavioral regression. If this is intentional V2 design, it should be documented.
